inputs.xtext_rule_text:
PayloadParameter returns SysML::ReferenceUsage :
	  Payload
	| Identification? PayloadFeatureSpecializationPart? TriggerValuePart
;

notes: re-scoped from the shared unit to sysml alone (ADR-0015)
decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.4. The Xtext differs in two ways and neither is a disagreement. It names its first alternative Payload, a rule that appears in no specification clause, where the clause writes PayloadFeature, which is a production with its own unit; the clause's name is taken. And it writes `Identification?` where the clause writes `Identification`, which is redundant rather than wider, because Identification is `( '<' NAME '>' )? ( declaredName = NAME )?` (8.2.2.2) and so already derives empty — the MultiplicityRange@kerml case again, and no deviation. The second alternative is what carries a timed or change trigger: TriggerValuePart is mandatory there, which is what separates `accept sig after 10[SI::s]` from the plain payload of `accept S`.

evidence.note: States the production; the rule is its transcription. The pack flags this clause as malformed, but the defect is in TriggerExpression (SYSML21-401) and not in this production.

Line 17 `then accept S;` takes the PayloadFeature alternative. Line 18 `then accept sig after 10[SI::s];` takes the second: `sig` is the Identification and `after 10[SI::s]` the TriggerValuePart. Line 22 `then accept when b.f;` takes the second with no Identification at all, which is what the nullability of Identification allows.
Second opinion. Same two alternatives; its Payload appears in no clause and its `Identification?` is redundant.
